summary: BIA 60-foot Aermotor tower on the Qualla Boundary, built 1957 to replace a 1930s wooden tower; unused since the 1960s; cab in poor shape; access reports conflict.

facts.design: 60-foot steel Aermotor tower with a 7-by-7-foot metal cab
facts.status_note: Standing but in poor condition: a 2018 visitor found the cab looking about to fall down and railings missing; a trail guide says half the cab floorboards are missing.
facts.agency: Bureau of Indian Affairs (Eastern Cherokee Agency cooperator, per Register)

access.note: On the Qualla Boundary (Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians land). A 2018 blog (July 2018) found a chain-link fence barring entry. An undated trail guide says the tower remains open to the public, but the same guide carries a May 2018 update: BIA Forestry rebuilt the chain-link fence around the base of the tower and closed it until further notice. No later access record found; sources disagree.

visit.trail_note: Hike from the Fire Mountain Trail System, minutes from downtown Cherokee: 2.4 to 2.6 miles and about 1,600 feet of climb, depending on the source. Sources disagree on whether the tower is open (the trail guide's May 2018 update says it was closed until further notice), and the cab floor is missing boards. Do not climb past a fence.

events.note: Built by the Bureau of Indian Affairs (Register; 2018 blog; trail guide)
Replaced a wooden tower dating from the 1930s (Register; 2018 blog)
Used for fire detection 'until the 1960s' per the 2018 blog, which cites Peter Barr's book. Approximate.
Register: unused for many years; the BIA and a North Carolina division of the Forest Fire Lookout Association were working on a restoration plan. No restoration found in later sources.
Registered April 2, 2008; nominated by Peter J. Barr

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 2018 blog (July 2018) says a chain-link fence bars entry and the cab is unsafe. An undated trail guide says the tower remains open to the public, but the same guide's May 2018 update says BIA Forestry rebuilt the fence and closed the tower until further notice. No tribal or agency access rule was found. The story reports both and does not choose.
The 2018 blog gives 2.4 miles uphill; the trail guide gives 2.6 miles. Both give about 1,600 feet of gain. The story reports both.

sources.title: Mount Noble Lookout Tower, Qualla Boundary, NC

notes_for_editor: Access is the main open question: the 2018 blog says fenced, and the undated trail guide says open, but its own May 2018 update says the fence was rebuilt and the tower closed until further notice. Verify with the tribe or the Fire Mountain Trail System managers before publishing. The 1957 build and BIA ownership match across the Register, the 2018 blog and the trail guide. The 1960s end of fire use rests on one blog that cites Peter Barr's book; not checked against the book. Restoration plan (2008) has no later record. Facebook posts that call the tower abandoned, and the Grokipedia page, are not cited. The Wikipedia 'Mount Noble' article is about an Antarctic peak and was not used. Read budget: 3 distinct pages and 2 searches. Height 60 ft converted to 18.3 m.
